titleEn: Interested in Investing in a Promising O2O Startup
contentEn:
1. Korea's Representative O2O Startup, Wyper

Following Cyworld, Wyper is the second company to attract investment interest on Wadiz, and I'd like to share its story. I've previously shared a link introducing Wyper, but this time it's introduced via a broadcast video, making it easy to understand.

http://blog.naver.com/fstory97/220408564204
                                [**[Delivery Car Wash Wyper] Don't worry about hand car washes when you're too busy to die** 1. Why O2O? Now there's no business unrelated to software. Until recently, all startups were social net... blog.naver.com](http://blog.naver.com/fstory97/220408564204)

In '[[Infographic] Everything about Korea's O2O](http://www.mobiinside.com/kr/index.php/2016/05/13/korea-o2o-1/)' published by Mobiinside, Wyper is listed as a representative O2O company in the car wash sector in Korea.

{{IMG:1}}
                                
                            Car Wash O2O Company Wyper, featured in '[Infographic] Everything about Korea's O2O'

2. Korea's Representative O2O Startup is Up for Sale.

I've used a somewhat provocative title for the second section, but I'm introducing this opportunity because shares of such a famous startup are available for purchase. Of course, if you buy 1 share, the allocation is 0.0008%, and the maximum number of shares to be issued is 1.0985%. If you invest the maximum amount, you can secure about 1% ownership for approximately 50 million won. Of course, this doesn't mean you can buy it outright, as it won't exceed 50%. However, at this point, it's closer to angel investment or VC funding than crowdfunding. In any case, there are virtually no ways for non-professional investors to purchase startup shares, and even professional investors require significant coordination with the company itself. However, this type of crowdfunding allows the public to easily participate in small-scale investments, aiming for a high-risk, high-return effect, while the company itself can secure funding and achieve marketing effects.

https://www.wadiz.kr/web/wprogram/detail/336
                                [**Wyper, who goes to the hand car wash for me** Please crowdfund Wadiz www.wadiz.kr](https://www.wadiz.kr/web/wprogram/detail/336)

If it were to be acquired by a large corporation like Kakao, or if the lifestyle of the entire nation shifted from visiting car washes directly to using O2O platforms, causing the market size to grow rapidly, the company's value could grow just as quickly. That's precisely the advantage of internet service companies.

3. Disappointments with Wadiz Crowdfunding: Complex Procedures

The advantage of crowdfunding is light investment. Treating it like pocket money, or investing a small amount in a good company doing great things, might even be a much higher-probability lottery. However, what I felt when encountering this service was its inconvenience. Even during the Cyworld investment, there were difficulties like creating a securities account, but this time, even if you have a securities account, the registration process requires scanned copies of paper documents, making it seem not easy to start. It seems to demand the same level of effort as opening a bank account. I just want to spend my own money... ㅜㅜ

{{IMG:2}}

I don't understand why they separately require proof of identity like a driver's license or resident registration card scan when there are online authentication methods like mobile carrier authentication or universal digital certificates. For an online system, making it feel so 'offline' like this feels like a very significant hurdle. If this is due to regulations, I think they should be boldly removed.

4. Despite the Difficulty of Purchase, It's Selling Like Hotcakes

I was worried that many wouldn't invest due to these inconveniences, but only 6 days have passed out of a total subscription period of 47 days, and 31% has already been achieved. At this rate, 100% will be easily reached. This means that many people see its high potential. My only regret is that if Wadiz's investment process were much simpler, companies might have received more benefits from such crowdfunding. People abandon shopping carts if they're inconvenient; these steps before investing might be a way to make people give up on investing altogether. For the sake of discovering promising companies, I hope these aspects are improved quickly.

My child is starting school next year, and with the skyrocketing jeonse prices, we recently moved. After moving and unpacking, I'm getting into a new mindset. Then my wife said, "When was the last time you exercised?" Even while I was looking into healthcare and such, my belly was still accumulating 'debt'. I told myself, "Even with this belly, I've exercised before, so it's fine." But since it had been a long time since I exercised, I was actually a little worried. Of course, my weight had also increased a bit (?). Then I got the chance to be a tester for a smart scale. It's called the Yunmai Smart Scale. The app for Xiaomi's Mi Scale had some issues, as I had to find and use a separate Chinese app, which sometimes disconnected. This smart scale is being sold by Komatrade, the official distributor for Xiaomi. I've been using it for about a week, and it feels quite good. I'm sharing the details.

**1. The Yunmai Smart Scale is as light as your body weight**

Yunmai Box: Simple packaging to save on cost as much as on weight.

It's cheap. The price is **currently 26,500 won.** Welcome, **Korean!** I hope my weight becomes this light too...

Much more luxurious than its price... This is the power of China these days ㅜㅜ It looks like this. Somehow, it feels a bit more distracting than the Xiaomi scale (Mi Scale), especially those 'yeonji-gonji' dots... However, there's a reason for those 'yeonji-gonji' dots.

**2. Comparison with Xiaomi Scale**

Simply put, it's smaller, lighter, and thinner. The color is slightly beige. While the Mi Scale is known for its extreme minimalism, this one is also quite sleek.

3. App Installation and Bluetooth Connection

Go to Google Play and search for "YUNMAI".

[**YUNMAI - Android Apps on Google Play** play.google.com](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.yunmai.scaleen)

No need to worry if the app description is in English. Once installed, it's in Korean. After installing the app, you need to register. You only need one registration per family, not one for each member. You can add family members to one account. In other words, my wife can see my weight changes.

{{IMG:1}}
https://blog.naver.com/PostView.naver?blogId=fstory97&logNo=223833999275&redirect=Dlog&widgetTypeCall=true&noTrackingCode=true&directAccess=false#

After logging into your account, set your height, age, and target weight, then step on the scale with Bluetooth turned on. **You don't need to manually pair the scale in the Bluetooth menu.**

**4. Body Fat, Skeletal Muscle Mass, Basal Metabolic Rate, and even Body Age**

The reason for those 'yeonji-gonji' dots is where you place your two feet. As soon as you step on it and your weight appears, a white bar progresses, measuring body fat, BMI, and body age. You can check the results in the app.

Most values are R-rated

A bit shocking... It shows scores, and nothing is right except for skeletal muscle mass. Body age comes out as "큰편" (big side) rather than "많은편" (many side), which seems like a translation error. I prided myself on looking a bit younger than my age, so I didn't expect it to be this bad... I have no excuses left for my wife.

{{IMG:2}}
https://blog.naver.com/PostView.naver?blogId=fstory97&logNo=223833999275&redirect=Dlog&widgetTypeCall=true&noTrackingCode=true&directAccess=false#

**5. Adding People**

To add a person, an add menu appears when someone with a significantly different weight steps on the scale. Alternatively, after adding a user, activate them and step on the scale for automatic setup. However, children cannot be added as it requires a minimum height of 120cm. I assume this is because children grow rapidly, making accurate measurements difficult. Therefore, when my son and daughter step on it, their data isn't separately recorded, but measurements are still possible.

**6. Changed Lifestyle**

After being a bit shocked by the results, I increased my morning stretches and walking distance. I also started being a little more careful about what I eat... And after that...

Hope is in sight.

{{IMG:3}}
https://blog.naver.com/PostView.naver?blogId=fstory97&logNo=223833999275&redirect=Dlog&widgetTypeCall=true&noTrackingCode=true&directAccess=false#

This is the motivation I needed. Before spending money on a gym, I recommend buying the Yunmai scale first. **At this price, it could even be given away for free when people sign up for a gym membership and used to manage members.**

{{IMG:4}}
https://blog.naver.com/PostView.naver?blogId=fstory97&logNo=223833999275&redirect=Dlog&widgetTypeCall=true&noTrackingCode=true&directAccess=false#

**The trainer is watching...** Above all, I was surprised by the cost-effectiveness of Xiaomi's Mi Scale, but this one easily surpasses Xiaomi. I heard that imports were banned due to the 'kg' unit display, so I'm curious how Yunmai, which has been handled by the Korean distributor this way, will respond. In addition to this, I'm currently using Sony's SWR30 SmartBand Talk. Based on this, I'm tracking how much I walk and how much I sleep, and a feature of this app is that it provides insights. I learned that I sleep much later and less than others. Currently, there's not much, but I wonder if it could even coach me on exercise volume. If a standard is established in the future, perhaps data exchange between Yunmai and SmartBand Talk could enable more efficient coaching. This is probably what healthcare AI is dreaming of. IoT was noisy for a while, but now it seems like products are emerging that actively collect data like this. Recently, several IoT products that I need to introduce arrived all at once. In reality, it seems to take about 1 to 2 years for an issue to become a complete and refined product. IoT seems to be just getting started. **P.S. I received only the product as compensation for this review, having been selected as a tester.**

titleEn: The Conflict Between Men and Women Might Be More Complex Than
contentEn:
Even amidst a hectic day at work today, I found myself at the center of a misogyny debate on Facebook. After several discussions, I came to realize that this issue might not be so simple. Even as I write this, I'm cautious, and although I've failed to organize my thoughts perfectly, I'd like to share some of my thoughts.

1. The Gangnam Station Murder Case and My "Kim Yeosa" Remark

Regarding whether the current situation surrounding the Gangnam Station murder case is excessive, I agree that it is not. I believe this incident serves as a trigger, offering a good opportunity to innovate and address underlying societal problems. Change and innovation are not born from lukewarm responses. Even when a ship carrying hundreds of students sinks, the path to innovation still feels long. Today's Facebook controversy stemmed from a comment I made, using "Kim Yeosa" as a theme, under a post expressing anger at people who don't use turn signals. First, to offer a slight excuse, my comment was not intended to demean women. However, many women seemed to think otherwise. So, after the controversy, I thought about it more deeply. Initially, the direction of the comment's controversy attempted to argue that women have lower spatial or cognitive abilities, and that this is the basis for certain social perceptions. However, the counter-argument started to veer in a strange direction, claiming it was unscientific, and an argument ensued. But upon reflection, this argument was misguided from the start. The perception of a word cannot be the same for the speaker and the listener. (Women's argument) Even if the speaker's intention was not that, the listener can still feel offended, and (Men's argument) whether the speaker's intention was truly not that, are two separate issues. Because both individuals made judgments based on their own confirmation biases in their brains, and merely stated their own positions. In fact, in the brain, what the truth is doesn't matter much. If there is only one truth, it is simply the fact that everything must be doubted. Therefore, regardless of the intention, it is necessary to consider both the speaker's and the listener's perspectives, and consequently, it is right for the person who ended up in the position of the 'offender' to apologize and be cautious, which is why I apologized and decided to be more careful with such remarks. Within the brain, a single word is defined based on countless experiences. It's similar to how AlphaGo learns Go moves. In my case, when I first encountered the 'Kim Yeosa' issue in an old online community, most members were male, and the first thing that came to mind was the 'Scooter Ajumma' episode from 'You're Under Arrest!' (체포해버리겠다). It was a cliché of a typical, pushy, shameless, nuisance 'ajumma' (middle-aged woman). Some young women might also agree that such clichés exist about older women. In fact, it's a cliché that frequently appears in media, just without using the specific term 'Kim Yeosa'. Even if not all older women are like that, and even if it actually reflects one aspect of our mothers, I believe... Even simple issues that we categorize as 'men vs. women' can be quite complex, requiring consideration of culture and the spirit of the times. Perhaps the reason the 'Kim Yeosa' remark is offensive is also because it aligns with the character of a shameless and helpless woman that one dislikes? Conversely, if I were to think of it from a male perspective, the fact that I align with the 'gaejeossi' (a derogatory term for rude, often older men) 'kkondae' (a condescending elder) character would not feel good.

2. Are Men and Women Truly Biologically Equal? Or Are You and I Equal?

Today, science has shattered many prejudices. It has proven that Black people and women are not biologically inferior to men. However, it has also begun to uncover those differences. And it has revealed that traits are influenced not only by biological factors but also by a complex interplay of environmental factors. The recent development of precision medicine utilizing AI aims to identify differences that consider genes, environment, and individual habits, rather than group-based medical care, and to provide appropriate services accordingly. The most basic hypothesis here is not that all individuals are the same, but that in fact, all are different. Disease is not the result of a single cause, but a complex interplay of various factors. Furthermore, how groups operate is even more complex. This is what is known as a complex system. Individuals are also composed of intelligence formed by conflicting experiences, and there are even theories that emotions are products of intelligence. Since groups are made up of such individuals, they are naturally more complex. To confess, I probably possess elements of a 'gaejeossi'. I won't deny it. The Japanese manga and anime I mentioned earlier often contain what could be called a 'gaejeossi' perspective. However, I don't believe such elements are exclusive to anime or manga produced as media commodities. I also see EDPS (a slang term for lewd jokes among computer science students), which was common among male students I didn't particularly like at the time, as such an element. What's interesting is that explicit sexual objectification and sexual abuse content exist in subcultures for both men and women. Of course, I oppose its use as a means to justify sexual violence, like Ilbe or Megal, and I consider it abnormal. Ultimately, the scientifically confirmed fact is only that the actual groups we know are not clear, and complex parameters are influencing each other. Therefore, it might not be possible to extract a single factor to explain communities like Megal and Ilbe, or the interpretations of the far-right represented by Trump and Abe, and perhaps opposing organizations or individuals are influencing each other through a multitude of butterfly effects?

3. Ultimately, There Is No Conclusion. Don't We Need to Objectify It More?

You might have expected a grand conclusion in my writing. However, there is no conclusion. I haven't been able to organize my thoughts either. The only confirmed fact is that such groups exist and are fighting. And that everyone, just like me, is not free from such prejudices. This exists not only in issues between men and women but also in religion, politics, or even within companies and families. I hope that the recent advancements in software development might offer some answers to this. Some say what we need now is empathy, and while empathy is certainly the most effective skill in conflict, I also believe that empathy itself might be the result of certain factors. Therefore, wouldn't a simpler or more fundamental approach be to bring empathy out of the realm of non-science and into the realm of science, and to find models that mediate and resolve conflicts? Of course, I also fight with my wife... planners fight with developers... elders fight with children... that's how we all live. The fortunate thing is that humanity, even if it loses a fight, doesn't live in a dog-eat-dog world where it devours its opponent. I wonder if the time has come to understand the human brain, humanity's greatest skill. Perhaps that will be one of the moments when humanity passes a singularity, successfully understanding itself. If I were having this conversation with my friend over drinks, he would probably say this: "Shut up and drink. That's why you never had a girlfriend. Be grateful to your wife." I wonder if some perverted engineering students like me would fail a Turing test if liberal arts female students administered it. Haha. Women are great, and in fact, I think the first thing that could be replaced by computers is actually men who are solely immersed in such logical thinking. To cool your head, here's the opening of 'You're Under Arrest!' (체포하겠어). It's a manga that instilled in me not only the image of 'Kim Yeosa' but also the romance of small cars.
